qualification: Cloudflare Access as the OIDC provider for the Cloudflare package (live round trip)

notes.accessPolicyDenial: An address outside every Access policy reaches the same 'enter your code' screen (no enumeration) and never receives a code, so the login cannot complete.
notes.preAdmissionRefusal: Access authenticates the identity; /auth/callback answers 403 IDENTITY_ADMISSION_DENIED, sets no session cookie, and the member list is unchanged.
notes.accessDiscovery: The Access discovery document reports code_challenge_methods_supported as null; the server's PKCE S256 flow completed regardless.
notes.contentHostRefusesApplicationRoutes: Checked on a token-shaped content host: /api/projects, /mcp and /auth/login answer 404 VERSION_NOT_FOUND or 405.

findings.summary: The content domain must be covered by an edge certificate for one wildcard level. A content domain nested under a shared zone (*.content.example.com) has no Universal SSL certificate and every content request fails the TLS handshake; the zone apex of a dedicated domain works with the free certificate. The Cloudflare README does not say this.

alchemy deploy from a fresh checkout fails with ENOENT dist/web: the Worker serves the web build as assets, but only pnpm check (pretest) builds it. The README deploy steps should build @artifact-server/web first, or the stack should.
An identity that Access authenticates but the server has not admitted sees raw JSON (403 IDENTITY_ADMISSION_DENIED) at /auth/callback instead of a readable page.
A login started directly at /auth/login (no return path) can land on /api/v1/session JSON after the callback instead of the review application.
Cloudflare Access SaaS OIDC applications do not reuse an existing Access session for a new authorization: a one-time-PIN user receives a new code on each login.
